os_limits.vm_swapusage: 0.00M used / 0.00M free (encrypted swap, none in use)

fd_safety_denominator.decision: kern.maxfilesperproc (61440) is the binding per-process ceiling, not the much larger soft ulimit -n

sampler_policy.rss: ps -o rss= -p <pid>, 1Hz, adopted for Mock/k6 this Unit and as the future Gateway candidate
sampler_policy.fd_non_java: lsof -p <pid> | wc -l, 1Hz this Unit (Mock/k6); ~30ms overhead per call on a small process
sampler_policy.fd_java_gateway: prefer Micrometer's own process_files_open_files (confirmed exported, Unit 2) -- no external sampler process needed
sampler_policy.cpu_java_gateway_formula_candidate: avg_cores ~= process_cpu_usage * system_cpu_count (both confirmed exported Unit 2) -- NOT yet cross-checked against real load, deferred to Unit 4

two_leg_connection_caveat: Direct Mock control (this Unit) exercises only ONE connection leg (k6 -> Mock). Future Gateway tests add a SECOND leg (Gateway -> Mock) plus the k6->Gateway leg, meaning FD/ephemeral-port pressure per logical stream roughly doubles compared to what this Unit measured. This is NOT fully proven safe by Direct Mock control alone -- carried forward as an explicit limitation, not resolved this Unit.
cooldown_policy: 5s between levels; fresh Mock process per level (no in-process state carryover); TIME_WAIT sockets from the prior level may still be draining when the next level starts -- captured as diagnostic snapshot only, no active draining, no OS TCP sysctl tuning performed
